messages:
taylor: heads up — i merged the lock regen PR earlier and now ubuntu-py310 job is red in CI :grimacing:
ci-bot: build/ubuntu-py310 #3421 FAILED in step 'pip wheel build'
ci-bot: error snippet:
```
  Building wheels for collected packages: pyrsistent
  Running setup.py bdist_wheel for pyrsistent ... error
  ERROR: Failed building wheel for pyrsistent
  Running setup.py clean for pyrsistent
  Failed to build pyrsistent
  ERROR: Could not build wheels for pyrsistent, which is required to install pyproject.toml-based projects
```
taylor: minimal repro locally with same base image shows same pip wheel error for pyrsistent 0.19.7 (previously pinned to 0.19.4 in our lock)
sam: ugh. was there a direct bump in our pyproject or is this transitive?
courtney: looks transitive — lock diff shows new resolver picked up pyrsistent 0.19.7 pulled by jsonschema->attrs chain i think
jyoti: can someone try `pip wheel --no-binary=:all: pyrsistent==0.19.7` in the job container? curious if build toolchain on CI is missing a header
alex: running quick repro now in dev container — same failure: extension build uses C99 flags and fails with "error: unknown type name 'whatever'" (truncated) — looks like wheel needs a newer wheel tag (manylinux) that upstream changed
nmorgan: (note: morgan out for the afternoon, but leaving this here) if it's a pure wheel change maybe temporary pin to 0.19.4 in constraints while we triage? :+1:
taylor: agree — want a quick mitigation. courtney, can you run a lock bisect? i can revert if bisect points to lock regen commit
courtney: yep i can do a bisect. which range? last green on main was 4112230000 per build history
courtney: plan: git checkout main~; then apply incremental lockfile chunks until we repro. will post small script if i need help
sam: if bisect shows transitive, we should also open an issue upstream for pyrsistent wheels on manylinux images — may be a packaging regression
jyoti: also flagging that windows/macos jobs are fine — this is only failing in linux-musl/manylinux CI runner (ubuntu image). maybe our builder lacks a newer gcc/pybind11 thing
alex: temporary patch: adding `pyrsistent = "==0.19.4"` to poetry.dev-dependencies constraints and running `poetry lock --no-update` prevented the failure locally. we can push a tiny commit to unblock CI if folks agree
taylor: go ahead and open PR with the pin + explanation. mark as temporary and link this thread. we'll follow up after courtney's bisect
courtney: starting bisect now. ping me if you want to help run steps or I should assign someone to iterate faster
morgan: thanks team — if we pin, let's include a TODO in the PR to remove after upstream fix or next lock regen with new wheel availability
sam: noted. i'll draft the upstream issue for pyrsistent packaging and attach the CI logs
taylor: awesome. i'll keep watch on CI and cancel other runs to reduce noise. thanks :pray:
